items.version: Current FDA vancomycin hydrochloride injection labeling at cited DailyMed set ID; live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: CDC — Collect Adult Blood Culture Sets, collection procedure: identify the patient with unique identifiers; disinfect the venipuncture site using an appropriate alcohol-containing skin disinfectant and allow it to dry; disinfect bottle septa; collect separate sets from separate venipuncture sites when possible.
items.version: CDC Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination guidance dated 2026-03-31; current federal guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.source_name: ARUP Laboratories — Wound Culture and Gram Stain
items.locator: ARUP Test 0060132, Wound Culture and Gram Stain — Specimen Required: collect aspirate/purulent material or a swab specimen from the wound; swab specimens are placed in the laboratory-designated ESwab transport medium. Anaerobic culture requires appropriate deeper specimen/transport when indicated.
items.version: Current ARUP Laboratories test directory entry 0060132; collection requirements live-rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected to Reduction of Risk Potential because the item tests collection of a nonblood diagnostic specimen, an explicit 2026 NCSBN laboratory-values activity.
items.stem: A provider orders an aerobic culture from an open draining wound. Which specimen-collection approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Scrape dried drainage from intact skin beside the wound and submit it in a dry container because surface material is the preferred culture source.
options.B: Swab the removed dressing because organisms on an old dressing represent the wound more accurately than material collected from the wound itself.
options.C: Swab intact periwound skin because normal skin flora identify the organism responsible for infection within the draining wound.
options.D: Collect purulent material or a specimen directly from the wound with the laboratory-approved sterile system and place it in the designated transport medium.

items.rationale: ARUP's wound-culture collection instructions call for purulent material/aspirate or a swab specimen collected from the wound and placed in the designated transport system. Option D samples the actual wound rather than old dressing material or intact surrounding skin. Options A, B, and C preferentially sample surface contamination or normal flora and do not follow the laboratory collection method. NCSBN places obtaining nonblood specimens for diagnostic testing under Reduction of Risk Potential.

items.locator: The Joint Commission — Two Patient Identifiers: Understanding the Requirements, FAQ updated 2026-04-21: use at least two person-specific identifiers; specimen containers must be labeled with two identifiers in the patient's presence; prelabeling blood tubes before seeing the patient is not acceptable; room number/location is not an acceptable identifier.
items.version: Joint Commission standards FAQ last updated 2026-04-21; current requirements live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: The Joint Commission — Two Patient Identifiers: Understanding the Requirements, FAQ updated 2026-04-21: acceptable identifiers are person-specific (for example name, date of birth, assigned identification number, telephone number); room number or physical location is not acceptable; organizations define their approved process.
items.version: Joint Commission standards FAQ last updated 2026-04-21; current requirements live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS — Check-Back (Repeat-Back): a closed-loop communication strategy in which the sender initiates a message, the receiver accepts and repeats it back, and the sender verifies/corrects the information to confirm shared understanding.

items.source_name: DailyMed — HUMULIN R (insulin human) injection, Eli Lilly
items.locator: DailyMed HUMULIN R — Dosage and Administration §2.2, Intravenous Administration: administer HUMULIN R intravenously ONLY under medical supervision with close monitoring of blood glucose and potassium; for IV use, use concentrations 0.1 unit/mL to 1 unit/mL in infusion systems containing 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection.
items.version: DailyMed HUMULIN R label updated 2025-05-27; §2.2 IV administration requirements live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A provider prescribes an intravenous HUMULIN R (regular insulin) infusion for a hospitalized client. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Prepare the prescribed IV concentration in 0.9% sodium chloride and monitor blood glucose and potassium closely during the infusion.
options.B: Use the U-100 vial concentration directly in the IV line because dilution is required only for subcutaneous insulin administration.
options.C: Monitor blood glucose closely but omit potassium monitoring because intravenous regular insulin does not affect serum potassium.
options.D: Prepare the infusion in any concentration selected by the nurse because the label gives no concentration range for intravenous use.

items.rationale: Current HUMULIN R labeling permits IV administration only under medical supervision, requires close monitoring of blood glucose and potassium, and specifies IV concentrations of 0.1 to 1 unit/mL in infusion systems containing 0.9% sodium chloride. Option A follows those labeled requirements. Option B incorrectly uses the U-100 vial concentration directly for IV infusion. Option C omits required potassium monitoring and falsely denies insulin-related hypokalemia risk. Option D ignores the labeled IV concentration range.
items.finding: Fresh Rule 1 audit identified two defects in the prior version: the stem explicitly stated a facility double-check policy that cued the keyed action, and the pharmacology claim relied on a medication-safety secondary source instead of the FDA-label hierarchy. The item was rewritten around DailyMed §2.2 IV HUMULIN R administration, then re-read for single-best-answer validity, distractor plausibility, cueing, source support, and NCLEX Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies alignment.
